title: [bug] BeautifulSoup HTML/EPUB extraction inserts newlines inside inline headings and code tokens
body: ## What happened The BeautifulSoup text conversion inserts a newline between **every text node**, including nodes separated only by inline styling. A span inside a heading, word, or syntax-highlighted code block changes the extracted content. This affects two current paths with the same cause: - HTML: the bs4 fallback when Trafilatura is unavailable or does not return usable content. - EPUB: the preferred ebooklib + bs4 parser. This path does not use Trafilatura. On unmodified master, a synthetic two-chapter source using `Chapter 1 ` produces **0 detected chapters**. Removing only the span markup produces 2. The styled source still exits successfully through the full CLI, including HTML `--mode technical`. For code, this source: ```html if enabled: print ("ok") ``` becomes: ```text if enabled: print ("ok") ``` Compiling that extracted snippet raises `IndentationError`; the same snippet without the styling spans, and the current stdlib output for this fixture, compile successfully. No extracted code was executed. ## What you expected Inline presentation markup should leave text continuous: `Chapter 1: Syntax`, `hypertext`, and the original code lines/indentation. Structural boundaries should still separate headings, paragraphs, lists and table rows; table cells need their own separators. The result should not depend on whether a chapter number or code token is wrapped in an inline element. ## Source document - Formats: synthetic HTML and EPUB 3; English; two content chapters.

title: BeautifulSoup Version
body: ### Symptom `usdm4.utility.soup.get_soup()` logs a Debug entry for most plain-text inputs that contain a `/`: Warning raised within Soup package, processing 'Known allergy/ incompatibility against deucravacitinib' Message returned 'The input looks more like a filename than markup. You may want to open this file and pass the filehandle into Beautiful Soup.' Protocol text is full of `and/or`, `U/kg`, `HIV 1/2`, `PaO2/FiO2`, so every protocol gets dozens of these. The same applies to anything else calling `get_soup`, including `tag_resolver.py`. ### Cause Not a usdm4 code bug. It's the bs4 version. In beautifulsoup4 1.2 U/kg` | warns | quiet | | `plain text` | quiet | quiet | usdm4 declares `beautifulsoup4>=4.9` in `setup.py` and `requirements.txt`. That floor lets existing environments stay on 4.12.x. ### Fix - `setup.py`: change `"beautifulsoup4>=4.9"` to `"beautifulsoup4>=4.13.1"` - `requirements.txt`: same change - Use 4.13.1, not 4.13.0. 4.13.0 was yanked from PyPI (wrong minimum Python pin). `get_soup()` itself doesn't change. It should keep logging whatever warnings bs4 raises. Only the false positives go away. ### Checks - Run the full test suite on bs4 >=4.13.1. 4.13 was a large release (type hints, some API tidy-up). Any usage of deprecated bs4 APIs should show up as failures or DeprecationWarnings. - Any expected-error fixtures that captured the `get_soup` Debug entries will need regenerating. ### Related usdm4_fhir issue #41 adds `beautifulsoup4>=4.13.1` to usdm4_fhi

title: Define the isolation guarantee for installed-wheel CI
body: Installed-wheel CI installs wheels, then runs tests from a checkout that may still contain package sources. There is an obvious trap: an import check run from the repository root can find the installed wheel, while a later test run from inside a package directory may import checkout code. A green job could then tell us less about the wheel than we think. We have not identified a false pass; this is a preventive question. [#2892](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuda-python/pull/2892) explored skipping source-dependent tests **when package sources are removed**. [#2949](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cuda-python/pull/2949) explored `python -I -m pytest` with an import-origin check inside each pytest process. [`-I`](https://docs.python.org/3.12/using/cmdline.html#cmdoption-I) keeps the working directory and `PYTHONPATH` off Python’s initial import path, addressing the most direct way checkout code can shadow a wheel while leaving source-tree tests available. However, this still falls short of isolation: * [pytest can alter `sys.path`](https://docs.pytest.org/en/stable/explanation/pythonpath.html) after Python starts, * tests can load checkout files directly, and * child processes do not automatically inherit `-I`. What should an installed-wheel job guarantee, and are import checks sufficient, or should package sources be made unavailable during those tests?

body: 0.2.3 is on PyPI. Publishing is release-only, uses Trusted Publishing with no stored token, and the wheel is installed and exercised before anything is uploaded (#33). What remains are the gaps that a release cannot recover from, because **PyPI never allows re-uploading a version, even after deletion**. ## Problem Five things are still wrong or unproven: 1. **No `LICENSE` file ships in the distribution.** `pyproject.toml` declares `license = "MIT"` and PyPI displays "MIT", but neither the sdist nor the wheel contains the licence text — and until #35 it did not exist in the repo either. A package that asserts a licence it does not carry is not redistributable by anyone who reads carefully. 2. **`policies/` is not in the wheel.** `stdtel-eval` grades the primary metric with OPA against `policies/`. Installed from PyPI there are no policies, so the only mode that works is `--dry-run` — which returns `True` for every policy. title: [ENH] `scikit-learn 1.9.X` compatibility
body: `sktime` currently has a few compatibility issues with `scikit-learn 1.9.X`, due to changes in the tag system. `scikit-learn` now assumes that wrapped estimators follow the same tag system. This is not on the level of framework, but on the level of estimators which internally wrap `sktime` objects in `sklearn` objects: * reducers `RecursiveTimeSeriesRegressionForecaster`, `DirectTimeSeriesRegressionForecaster`, `MultioutputTimeSeriesRegressionForecaster`, `DirRecTimeSeriesRegressionForecaster` * `TSRGridSearchCV` and `TSCGridSearchCV`, see #10724 * `ElasticEnsemble` The above incompatibilities should be investigated and fixed. For the grid searches, #10724 should be tracked.

title: OrionMSP fit crashes with sklearn>=1.8: check_X_y() got 'force_all_finite'
body: Fitting `OrionMSP` (via its sklearn `classifier.fit`) crashes on current scikit-learn versions: ``` TypeError: check_X_y() got an unexpected keyword argument 'force_all_finite' ``` This comes from `preprocessing.py`'s own `_validate_data` backport, which calls `sklearn.utils.validation.check_X_y(..., force_all_finite="allow-nan")` directly. That kwarg was renamed to `ensure_all_finite` and later removed in scikit-learn 1.8+. The file already has a sklearn-compat shim for `check_array` (imported from an internal `sklearn_compat` module) that handles this rename, but `check_X_y` is imported directly from `sklearn.utils.validation` instead of going through the same shim, so it doesn't get the same compatibility handling. Happy to share more details if useful.

body: ## Goal Declare current scikit-learn estimator tags for every public estimator and transformer so discovery, validation, and `check_estimator` exercise the correct dense, sparse, missing-value, and transformer contracts. ## Scope - Implement `__sklearn_tags__()` using the current `Tags` dataclass API and `super().__sklearn_tags__()`. - Set transformer and input tags from tested behavior, including two-dimensional input, sparse support, missing-value support, fitted-state requirements, and reproducibility. - Do not claim support based only on intended behavior; each non-default tag needs a focused test. - Pin a scikit-learn floor compatible with the chosen tag API rather than maintaining divergent `_more_tags` branches. ## Acceptance criteria - Tags exist for `VBPCA` and every exported preprocessing transformer. - Dense/sparse/NaN claims match focused behavior tests. - Relevant `check_estimator` checks are selected by the tags and pass in #39. - CI tests the minimum and current supported scikit-learn versions. Official contract: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/developers/develop.html#estimator-tags Depends on #36 and #38.
